newsitem.title: EGYPT: At least 15 dead in train crash in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: At least 15 dead in train crash in south Egypt.

text.p: At least 15 people were killed and 10 injured when a cargo train slammed into a passenger train near the southern Egyptian tourist town of Edfu on Monday, southern security sources said.
The interior ministry said in a statement that rescuers had so far pulled out nine bodies and that another eight people had been injured in the crash.

The sources said the passenger train, which was travelling from the Mediterranean city of Alexandria to the southern resort of Aswan, was stopped at the Radissiyah station when the cargo train rammed into its rear compartments.
Radissiya is about 600 km (375 miles) south of Cairo.
The sources said a railway worker at a village along the track had given the cargo train the go-ahead even though the passenger train had not yet pulled out of the station.
Rescue workers were still trying to remove the dead and injured from the two damaged rear cars of the passenger train, the sources said. The engine of the cargo train was also damaged, they added.
Seventy-five people were killed in 1995 when a passenger train collided full-speed into another train due to faulty signals at the Badrasheen station outside Cairo.
